title: Butkara I Stupa
subtitle: Buddhist stupa and votive court on the eastern edge of Mingora, Swat

landmark.name: Butkara I Stupa
edits: The excavated sacred area is drawn from the Atlas photos (Front View of the main stupa, Votive Stupa Court): a flagged court, the main stupa as a stepped circular base with a whitewashed lower drum and a broken upper drum, and four rings of votive stupas and stone bases (10, 16, 18 and 20 units) with column bases on the outer ring.

No published dimensions were found for the main stupa or the votive stupas (the Wikipedia article gives none). The main stupa's outer diameter (about 19 m), base steps, drum height (about 6 m) and ruined top (about 8 m) are ESTIMATED from the photos.

The votive stupa sizes (bases 2 to 3 m square, drums under 2 m across), the ring radii, the court wall and the paving are ESTIMATED from the photos. Their number and place are invented to read as the court, not surveyed.

The OSM building that is tagged as the site (tourism=museum, 36 m from the point) and every other building within 80 m are dropped and replaced by this model. The ground within 70 m is levelled (a terrace); the rest is the real DEM slope.
The earlier generic Atlas maquette (a ~22 m plinth with a ruined drum) is not used: it is not a record of this stupa.
